doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: The farcical union audition
summary: He returns after six months and passes an audition by identifying a piano; he comments on unionism protecting existing members.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Am I correct in saying the singers have to be in the actor’s guild?

No, they’ve got a separate union now, which is, I forget what it is because it doesn’t really concern me. But at that time, they had to be in the musician’s union. Otherwise they couldn’t work. It was very strongly unionized. So anyway, he says, “next.” So I go into this room, there’s the piano. And he says, “what’s that instrument over there?” I said, “what are you talking about?” I says, “a piano.” He says, “you’re in. Now go upstairs and pay your hundred dollars.” I said, “what?” I started roaring. He says, “that’s very nice, now go upstairs.”
Kind of makes you wonder about the level of musicianship that they might have in the unions.
I mean I’m all for auditions, but they should be serious.
Yeah, if you’re going to do it.
And they made you wait six months for that.

Well that was a thing to protect — it’s unionism at its worst. I think it was there to protect the jobs of people who were there. They didn’t want too many new people coming in and taking their jobs away. Not that I was about to take anybody’s job, but I just wanted to be a part of the scene.
